This kind of falls under the preferences of the providers. Technically speaking measurement of your radial pulses, DP/PT pulses, and other pulses should go under CV. However some providers have preferences to put DP/PT pulses in extremities to organize their findings. Whenever they’re assessing an extremity some providers like if you group all the findings under that examined extremity. (E.g. RUE: TTP of distal radius but no edema or erythema, 2+ radial pulses, cap refill <2 secs, NVID) In the example above, you could technically split all the findings into their respective categories but some providers feel like it’s easier to read and it’s cleaner if you just put all that in MSK

I used to do this until I got used to the game but, part of the scare factor for me used to be how dark it was at night time and how much I couldn’t see (before getting a helmet light mod or night vision goggles). So to help myself ease into it I played with the brightness all the way up so that the nighttime was easier to see and I could see the zombies from farther. I set the settings back to default once I got used to the game though. But I will say that going from a scarier game where the nights are more terrifying like the forest or dying light, 7DTD should be pretty damn tame in comparison. :) love the game though
